# Python Markdown

# A Python implementation of John Gruber's Markdown.

# Documentation: https://python-markdown.github.io/
# GitHub: https://github.com/Python-Markdown/markdown/
# PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/Markdown/

# Started by Manfred Stienstra (http://www.dwerg.net/).
# Maintained for a few years by Yuri Takhteyev (http://www.freewisdom.org).
# Currently maintained by Waylan Limberg (https://github.com/waylan),
# Dmitry Shachnev (https://github.com/mitya57) and Isaac Muse (https://github.com/facelessuser).

# Copyright 2007-2023 The Python Markdown Project (v. 1.7 and later)
# Copyright 2004, 2005, 2006 Yuri Takhteyev (v. 0.2-1.6b)
# Copyright 2004 Manfred Stienstra (the original version)

# License: BSD (see LICENSE.md for details).

"""
An extension to Python Markdown which adds `target="_blank"` and
`rel="noopener noreferrer"` to external links.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from markdown.treeprocessors import Treeprocessor
from markdown.extensions import Extension


class ExternalLinksTreeprocessor(Treeprocessor):
    """ Add `target` and `rel` attributes to external `a` elements. """

    def run(self, root):
        for el in root.iter('a'):
            href = el.get('href')
            if isinstance(href, str) and href.startswith(('http://', 'https://')):
                el.set('target', '_blank')
                el.set('rel', 'noopener noreferrer')


class ExternalLinksExtension(Extension):
    """ Add the external links tree processor to Markdown. """

    def extendMarkdown(self, md):
        md.treeprocessors.register(ExternalLinksTreeprocessor(md), 'external_links', 15)


def makeExtension(**kwargs):  # pragma: no cover
    """ Return an instance of the `ExternalLinksExtension` """
    return ExternalLinksExtension(**kwargs)

I made no code change, because this test conflicts with the spec. The core serializer (`markdown/serializers.py:178`) sorts attributes lexically, so `rel` is always written before `target`. Making the test pass would mean changing the serializer, and that would alter the output of every existing extension. The spec says attribute order is unspecified, and the design says to assert on attribute presence rather than order.

I did not re-run the tests this attempt. The failing output in the report matches the serializer behaviour.

TEST_DISPUTE: tests.test_syntax.extensions.test_external_links.TestExternalLinks.test_ac_fr_008_1_no_config_needed: AC-FR-008-1 only requires the output to match AC-FR-003-1, and the spec's findings say attribute order is unspecified. The test asserts an exact `href, target, rel` order, which the core serializer's lexical sorting (`href, rel, target`) makes impossible without a core change.
